Package frc.robot.subsystems.turret

Class Turret

java.lang.Object
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
frc.robot.subsystems.turret.Turret
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem
public class Turret extends edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
Turret subsystem â€” a single-axis yaw mechanism that rotates the shooter to face the hub.

Hardware Overview

The turret uses one TalonFX motor driving a gear reduction (TurretConstants.kGearRatio) with a single CANcoder absolute encoder for position. A single absolute encoder means no homing routine is needed after power-on â€” the turret knows its absolute angle immediately. The encoder's magnetic offset (TurretConstants.kEncoderConfig) is calibrated so that reading 0 corresponds to the turret facing directly forward on the robot.

Travel Limits

The turret can rotate between TurretConstants.kMinAngle (âˆ’0.5 rotations = âˆ’180Â°) and TurretConstants.kMaxAngle (+0.5 rotations = +180Â°). TalonFX software limits enforce this in hardware. The findCC(double, double, double, double) algorithm (see below) always chooses a target within these limits, so the motor never hits a soft-limit stop during normal tracking.

IO Layer

All hardware interaction goes through TurretIO. Three implementations exist:
  • TurretIOHardware â€” real robot (TalonFX + CANcoder).
  • TurretIOSim â€” WPILib simulation (simulated motor physics).
  • TurretIODisabled â€” no-op; used in disabled mode and test environments.
The active implementation is selected in RobotContainer based on Constants.RobotConstants.currentMode.

Motion Profile

The motor uses TalonFX MotionMagic in Slot 0: a trapezoidal velocity profile up to TurretConstants.kMaxSpeed rot/s with TurretConstants.kMaxAcceleration rot/sÂ². This gives smooth, controlled slewing without overshoot.

  • Constructor Details

    • Turret

      public Turret(TurretIO io)
      Constructs the turret, calibrates the encoder, and registers telemetry + SmartDashboard buttons.

      TurretIO.calibrate() reads the CANcoder absolute position and sets the TalonFX internal encoder to match, establishing the absolute reference. Calibration also runs automatically when the robot is disabled (via RobotModeTriggers.disabled()) to recover from any drift.

      Parameters:
      io - the hardware/sim/disabled implementation to use

    • track

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command track(StateManager state)
      Returns a command that continuously aims the turret at the scoring hub, accounting for robot rotation and ball lead compensation.

      Algorithm Each Loop Cycle

      1. Get the robot's current field-relative heading from StateManager.robotPose().
      2. Get lead-compensated shot parameters from StateManager.aimParams(), which runs the full LeadCompensator â†’ ToFAim pipeline.
      3. If the shot is feasible (AimParams.isOk()), compute the required turret angle: 
                 mechanismAngle = (fieldYaw âˆ’ robotHeading) + kForwards
        where fieldYaw is the field-frame direction to the hub, robotHeading is the robot's heading, and kForwards is the encoder offset for the forward direction. The subtraction converts field-frame to robot-relative, then kForwards maps "robot-forward" to the encoder's zero point.
      4. Set the position reference. The tracking flag passed to setPosition(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Angle, boolean) is true when the shot is not yet ready â€” this enables a wider position tolerance in the motion profile for faster slewing, tightening to the final tolerance only when the shooter is also at speed.

      The command uses run() so it repeats every loop. When it ends (trigger released or interrupted), tracking is set to false via finallyDo so the tracked(java.util.function.Supplier<frc.robot.aiming.AimParams>) trigger correctly reports not-tracking.

      Parameters:
      state - provides robot pose and aim parameters from the state machine

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command home()

      Home is defined by TurretConstants.kHomePosition. The command completes when ready() is true â€” i.e., when the turret is within TurretConstants.kTolerance of the reference.     • tracked

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.button.Trigger tracked(Supplier<AimParams> params)
      Returns a Trigger that is true when the turret is actively tracking (track(frc.robot.superstructure.StateManager) is running) AND within the aim tolerance specified in the current AimParams.

      The tolerance params.deltaYaw comes from the aim pipeline and can be tighter or looser depending on how accurate the shot needs to be at the current distance.

      Used by RobotStateMachine.isShootReady() (via the Shooter tracked trigger), which gates the hopper in ShootWhenReady.

      Parameters:
      params - supplier of current aim parameters; called each time the trigger is evaluated

    • turretPose

      public edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d turretPose(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d robotPose)
      Returns the current turret pose in field coordinates, composed from the robot pose and the fixed turret mounting offset (TurretConstants.kOffset).

      This 3D pose is used as the "shooter position" in the aiming pipeline so the aim solver computes angles from the actual launch point rather than the robot center.

      Parameters:
      robotPose - current field-relative robot pose from odometry/vision

    • jog

      public edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Command jog(double rotationsPerSecond)
      Returns a command that jogs the turret at a fixed speed by incrementing the position reference each loop cycle.

      Since the new Hackbots TurretIO interface only exposes position control (no direct voltage or speed command), manual jog is implemented as a small position step per loop: 

         reference += rotationsPerSecond Ã— 0.02 s     (0.02 s = one 50 Hz loop)
      This increments the reference smoothly at the specified angular rate, and MotionMagic follows it with the configured cruise velocity and acceleration. When the command ends (button released), the reference stops updating and the turret holds its last position.

      Bound to gunner POV right (+0.5 rot/s) and POV left (âˆ’0.5 rot/s) in RobotContainer. Soft limits in the TalonFX configuration prevent the turret from jogging past TurretConstants.kMinAngle or TurretConstants.kMaxAngle.

      Parameters:
      rotationsPerSecond - positive = counter-clockwise; negative = clockwise. Typical value Â±0.5 rot/s = Â±180Â°/s (reaches end of travel in ~1 s)

    • findCC

      protected static double findCC(double position, double reference, double min, double max)
      Returns the closest congruent value to position for a given reference angle, constrained to [min, max].

      What "Congruent" Means Here

      A single absolute encoder reports a value in [0, 1) rotations. But the physical turret can turn multiple full rotations (its range is about Â±0.5 rot = Â±180Â°). The motor encoder tracks total rotations (e.g., 2.3), not just the fractional part. Two angles are congruent if they differ by a whole number of rotations â€” they represent the same physical turret orientation.

      Why This Matters

      Suppose the turret is at 2.7 rotations and the desired orientation is 0.3 rotations (i.e., the same as 1.3, 2.3, 3.3, â€¦). The wrong choice is 0.3 â€” that requires driving from 2.7 almost back to 0 (a 2.4 rotation trip). The right choice is 2.3, which is just 0.4 rotations away. This avoids spinning the turret the "long way" and hitting a soft limit.

      Algorithm

      1. Bring the reference into [min, max] by adding or subtracting 1 rotation at a time.
      2. If still out of range, clamp to max.
      3. If the reference is already within 0.5 rotations of the current position, return it (it's already the closest congruent value).
      4. Otherwise, try shifting by Â±1 rotation toward the current position, stopping when we find the shift that puts the error below 0.5 rotations.

      This is a package-private static so it can be unit-tested independently of hardware.

      Parameters:
      position - current multi-turn encoder position (e.g., 2.7)
      reference - desired orientation as a fractional rotation in [0, 1) (e.g., 0.3)
      min - minimum allowed encoder position (e.g., âˆ’0.5)
      max - maximum allowed encoder position (e.g., +0.5)
      Returns:
      the closest value to position that is congruent to reference and within [min, max]

    • turretCameraOffset

      public edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Transform3d turretCameraOffset()
      Returns the transform from robot origin to the turret camera in field coordinates, accounting for the current turret angle.

      Used by the vision subsystem to transform camera observations into field coordinates. The transform is composed of:

      1. TurretConstants.kOffset â€” fixed robot-to-turret-base transform (from CAD).
      2. A rotation by the current turret angle around the yaw axis.
      3. LocalizationConstants.kTurretAoRToTurretCameraOffset â€” camera mounting offset on the turret (measured in Stage 8-2, currently a placeholder).
